# yaml-test-suite ledger — the expected outcome of THIS module on every case of
# github.com/yaml/yaml-test-suite (`data` branch), asserted by src/suite_test.zig.
#
# The suite itself is NOT vendored here (fetch it and point ZIG_LIBS_YAML_SUITE
# at it, or the harness skips loudly). This file is the committed claim about it.
#
# ONE ROW PER CASE, three columns, then an optional reason:
#
#   <id>  <events>  <json>  [reason]
#
# <events> — the Part 1 event layer, against `test.event`:
#   event    parses, and the dumped event stream equals test.event byte for byte
#   reject   the suite marks the input invalid (an `error` file); we must error
#   fail     KNOWN-FAIL against the above; a specific reason is mandatory
#
# <json> — the Part 2 compose + core-schema layer, against `in.json`:
#   json     composes, and the value tree equals in.json (type-exact: 1, 1.0 and
#            "1" are three different answers)
#   none     no oracle for this case — either the suite ships no in.json (its
#            YAML has non-string mapping keys, so it has no JSON form) or the
#            case is a must-reject one
#   fail     KNOWN-FAIL against in.json; a specific reason is mandatory
#
# Enforced in BOTH directions and cross-checked against the suite itself:
#   - a listed pass that fails is red; a listed KNOWN-FAIL that passes is red
#   - the id set must equal the suite's exactly
#   - `reject` must agree with the presence of an `error` file
#   - `json`/`fail` requires an in.json to exist; `none` requires it not to
#     (or the case to be must-reject)
#   - `events fail` forces `json none` — what does not parse cannot compose
#   - a `fail` in either column requires a non-empty reason
#
# 402 cases. Events: 402/402. JSON: 279 cases carry an oracle (282 in.json
# files, less the 3 that belong to must-reject cases); 29 non-error cases have
# no JSON form at all. Do not add a `fail` without a specific reason.
